Benchmark topology setup and command flow for development runs, including affinity checks and tile launch.

# Purpose
This file defines the `bench` command for the development control tool. It parses the `--no-quic` command-line option in [`bench_cmd_args`](<#bench_cmd_args>), then builds a benchmark topology in [`add_bench_topo`](<#add_bench_topo>) with `bencho`, `benchg`, and `benchs` tiles, workspace links, and CPU affinity mapping. The code also checks that the affinity string matches the number of benchmark tiles and that CPU indexes are valid for the host system. When the affinity is set to `auto`, it recomputes the topology layout with `fd_topob_auto_layout`.

The [`bench_cmd_fn`](<#bench_cmd_fn>) function prepares the full runtime configuration for a benchmark run. It selects the transaction listen port, sets the RPC port, checks that the layout affinity settings are consistent, and calls [`add_bench_topo`](<#add_bench_topo>) to attach the benchmark tiles to the topology. It then runs the normal configure flow, applies development updates, initializes Firedancer, sets up the network namespace, installs XDP if needed, joins shared workspaces, and starts the topology in single-process mode with [`fdctl_tile_run`](<#fdctl_tile_run>). This file therefore provides the entry point for a benchmark execution path and connects configuration, topology setup, and process start-up.
